def encode(self, text: str, add_special_tokens: bool = False) -> list[int]:
    """Tokenize UTF-8 with the GGUF vocabulary, preserving special-token and BOS handling."""
    raw = text.encode("utf-8")
    length = len(raw)
    add_bos = bool(add_special_tokens and self.add_bos)
    token_type = self.L.llama_token
    tokenize = self.L.llama_tokenize
    capacity = length + 16
    tokens = (token_type * capacity)()
    count = tokenize(self.vocab, raw, length, tokens, capacity, add_bos, True)
    if count < 0:
        capacity = -count
        tokens = (token_type * capacity)()
        count = tokenize(self.vocab, raw, length, tokens, capacity, add_bos, True)
        if count < 0:
            raise ValueError("llama.cpp could not tokenize the text")
    # Slicing an integer ctypes array already produces an independent Python list.
    return tokens[:count]
rationale: The measured function wraps an opaque native tokenizer. A ctypes integer-array slice already allocates and fills a new Python list, so list(slice) copies all token references a second time. Return the slice directly. Keep one private native buffer per call, the UTF-8 byte length, BOS/special flags and negative-size retry. This removes linear host work without retaining request text or token IDs between calls. The native tokenization itself may dominate end-to-end time.
